generationMode: one original full-canvas scene per call
style: Original black monochrome technical line illustration with confident medium contour, sparse functional hatching, restrained interior detail, generous whitespace, and plain civil-service test-booklet economy. Original subjects and compositions only; do not reconstruct any official sample.
globalExclusions: No text or pseudo-text; no readable signs, labels, letters, numbers, arrows, circles, answer marks, logos, brands, watermarks, decorative borders, color-only cues, cropped meaning-bearing objects, impossible joints or poses, duplicated people or parts, floating objects, dramatic spotlighting, or visual emphasis on the target.

sourceLines.excerpt: Work areas, passageways, and walking-working surfaces must be kept clean, orderly, and sanitary.
Workroom floors must be clean and, as far as feasible, dry.
Walking-working surfaces must remain free of hazards such as sharp objects, leaks, and spills.
Correct a hazardous surface before reuse, or guard it against use until corrected.
Wet floors, spills, and bunched coverings are recognized slip-or-trip conditions.
Clean spills promptly, correct bulged coverings, and keep routes clear.
Exit routes must remain unobstructed and contain no placed materials or equipment.
Exit-route requirements support safe evacuation during an emergency.
Handrails must be smooth, graspable, non-projecting, and meet specified strength criteria.
Hazard information is communicated through labels or warnings, safety data sheets, and training.
Coverage depends on a chemical known to be present with potential employee exposure.
Covered workplace containers require hazard identification, except qualifying immediate-use portable containers.
Existing incoming-container labels may not be removed or defaced unless immediately replaced.
Poisonous or toxic materials must be separated and not stored above food, equipment, or utensils.
Direct or adjacent poisonous-material storage can contaminate food or equipment through spillage.
Clean equipment and utensils must be stored dry, protected, and covered or inverted as applicable.
Portable equipment and cords must be handled without damaging their jacket or insulation.
Inspect cord-connected equipment for visible defects and remove hazardous damaged items from service.
Water-contact locations require approved equipment, and wet energized connections can create a conducting path.
Damaged cords with exposed conductors can cause shock, burns, or fire.
Wet cord connections can leak current through a person who supplies a path to ground.
Electrical hazards can cause shock, burns, fire, and fatal electrocution.
Broken glass encountered during cleanup can cause cuts.
Use a broom and dustpan instead of hands and use task-appropriate provided protection.
Material-handling aisles and passageways require safe clearance and must remain unobstructed.
Tiered containers must be stacked and height-limited to remain secure against sliding or collapse.

sourceLines.locator: Management Guidelines for Safer Carrying, PDF pp. 29-30
sourceLines.excerpt: For unstable or heavy loads, rebalance or reduce the load and use suitable mechanical or team assistance.

sourceLines.locator: Employee Guidelines for Safer Carrying, PDF pp. 30-31
sourceLines.excerpt: Avoid bulky loads that obstruct vision and keep a clear view of the route while carrying.
Promptly clean and decontaminate blood or potentially infectious-material spills under the proper procedure.
Use protective gloves and other protective equipment appropriate to the cleanup task.
Assess hazards and select protective equipment that protects against the identified exposure.
After use, mops must air-dry without soiling equipment or supplies.
Improperly cleaned or stored mops can contaminate food and preparation areas.
Contaminated wiping materials can transfer allergens; complete cleaning minimizes transfer among surfaces.
Guard moving parts and points of operation when machine operation exposes workers to injury.
Fan blades below seven feet require guards with openings no larger than one-half inch.
Covered portable circular saws require upper and lower guards; the lower guard must return automatically.
Inspect ladders, remove defective ones, lock stepladders open, and use them on stable surfaces protected from displacement.
Flexible cords used as temporary wiring must be supported and protected from accidental physical damage.

targetInventory.observableCondition: A wide shallow wet patch crosses the central walking path, and no warning control is visible.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The spill makes the travel surface non-dry and creates a recognized slip-and-fall condition.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: A person could slip, fall, and be injured.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Guard or close off the wet section, stop the source if one is present, and clean and dry the surface before reopening it.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: Fixed metal conduit runs tightly along the base of the right wall.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: A long object near floor level can resemble something that crosses the walking route or catches a foot.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: The conduit is fixed tight to the wall and remains outside the walking route; no loose or protruding condition is shown.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The conduit would become unsafe if it became loose, developed a sharp or projecting edge, or extended into the walking surface.

safeBackground: wall-mounted bulletin frame with blank interior
janitor cart fully inside a side alcove
requiredCues: wet patch visibly reflective by contour and hatch, not color
patch large enough to recognize at phone size
unobstructed view of the dry surrounding floor
scenes.neutralOverview: A school hallway with doors, a side alcove, and a long tiled walking surface.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape school hallway. A broad shallow irregular wet patch spans the lower-center walking path, visible through reflected contour lines and sparse hatching, with no warning cone or sign anywhere. A janitor cart is fully parked in a side alcove. Fixed metal conduit runs tightly along the base of the right wall and never enters the path. Keep the corridor otherwise clean, dry, and unobstructed.

targetInventory.observableCondition: One entrance-mat corner is visibly curled several inches upward in the walking route.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The raised mat edge interrupts the walking surface and can catch a foot.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: A person could trip, fall, and be injured.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Guard the affected area, then flatten, secure, reposition, or remove the mat so the route is even before reopening it.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: An umbrella stand is upright outside the travel lane.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: A movable stand near an entrance can look like an obstruction or source of tracked water.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: The stand is upright and outside the travel lane, and no spill or instability is shown.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The stand would become unsafe if it were placed or tipped into the route, or released water onto the floor.

requiredCues: clearly raised mat corner with visible gap and shadow line
dry surrounding floor
open walking route except for the mat edge
scenes.neutralOverview: A school entrance lobby with double doors, a floor mat, a wall bench, and an umbrella stand.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape school entrance lobby. A rectangular entrance mat lies in the walking route; one near corner is clearly buckled and curled upward with a visible gap under it. The tile floor is completely dry. Double entrance doors and their path are otherwise clear. A stable umbrella stand sits outside the travel lane and a bench is flush against the wall.

targetInventory.observableCondition: Several closed boxes occupy most of the stair landing and narrow the passage.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The boxes are materials placed within the exit route and reduce the usable landing passage.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: They could delay or prevent safe evacuation during an emergency.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Remove all stored material from the landing and restore the full continuous exit route.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: A continuous smooth handrail has intact brackets and no visible loose or projecting part.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: A wall-mounted rail projects beside the stair route and can initially resemble an obstruction.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: The rail is the intended stair-support feature, with no rough surface, hazardous projection, or visible damage shown.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The handrail would become unsafe if it were loose, rough or sharp, difficult to grasp, projected hazardously, or failed required strength.
decoyInventory.evidenceCaveat: The illustration does not certify hidden mounting strength or exact dimensions.

safeBackground: dry intact steps on the upper flight
dry intact steps on the lower flight
closed utility door outside the stair path
requiredCues: boxes visibly reduce usable landing width
continuous stair route visible around the obstruction
boxes stable and closed so the target is obstruction, not falling objects
scenes.neutralOverview: An enclosed school stairwell with two flights, a landing, wall handrails, and several boxes.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape cutaway view of an enclosed school stairwell. Several closed, stable cardboard boxes are stored across most of the central landing, leaving only a narrow passage between the upper and lower flights. Both flights are dry and intact, and both handrails are securely mounted. No other clutter appears.

targetInventory.observableCondition: Folded gym mats and an equipment cart are parked directly in front of the double doors and across their approach.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The mats and cart occupy the doorway approach and exit route.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: The obstruction could delay or prevent safe evacuation during an emergency.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Move the mats and cart outside the doorway and approach, restoring the full exit route.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: A basketball rack is parked stably against a side wall outside the doorway approach.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: A movable equipment rack can become an exit obstruction if parked in the wrong place.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: The rack is stable against a side wall and remains outside the doorway and exit route.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The rack would become unsafe if it were moved into the doorway, approach, or another part of the exit route.

requiredCues: panic-bar double doors visually recognizable without text
obstruction directly overlaps door swing and approach
side storage clearly outside travel route
scenes.neutralOverview: A school gym with a clear court, rear double doors, folded mats, and equipment storage.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape school gym. At the rear, double doors with plain horizontal panic bars are directly blocked by folded gym mats and a stable equipment cart parked across the doorway and approach. The remaining court is clear. Retracted bleachers and a basketball rack sit safely against side walls outside the route.

targetInventory.observableCondition: A plain working spray bottle holds an unknown liquid and has a completely blank body with no visible identification.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The pixels do not establish HazCom coverage or the immediate-use exception, so the unidentified liquid is a stop-and-verify condition rather than a proven labeling violation.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: Until the contents and status are verified, a worker may lack the product, hazard, and protective information needed for safe handling or response.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Stop non-immediate use and verify the contents and container status; if it holds a covered hazardous chemical, identify it under the workplace hazard-communication program before further use.
targetInventory.evidenceCaveat: A blank bottle does not prove that it contains a covered hazardous chemical or that the immediate-use exception is unavailable.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: Generic supply jugs are closed and upright in a low containment tray.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: Generic jugs in a custodial closet can resemble hazardous-chemical containers.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: No leak or instability is shown, and the drawing does not establish hazardous contents or missing required identification.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The jugs would require correction if they were established as covered hazardous-chemical containers and lacked required workplace identification, or an incoming label had been removed or defaced.
decoyInventory.evidenceCaveat: Closed, upright, contained storage does not by itself prove Hazard Communication compliance.

requiredCues: secondary bottle visibly contains liquid
bottle body wholly blank with no label panel or symbol
other containers closed and stable
scenes.neutralOverview: A custodial closet with shelving, a service sink, stored containers, a spray bottle, and secured cleaning tools.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape custodial closet. On the middle-left shelf sits one plain secondary spray bottle visibly half-filled with liquid; its entire smooth body is completely blank, with no label panel, symbol, or writing. Nearby generic supply jugs are closed, upright, and held in a low containment tray. A mop is secured in a wall rack, the service sink is empty, and the floor is dry.

targetInventory.observableCondition: Closed cleaning-supply bottles are stored on an open shelf directly above uncovered clean bowls and food-preparation utensils.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The authored scenario establishes that the bottles hold poisonous or toxic cleaning supplies; storage directly above uncovered bowls and utensils creates a path for spill or drip contamination.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: Spillage could contaminate the bowls or utensils and later contaminate food.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Move the cleaning supplies to designated storage separated by spacing or partitioning and not above food, equipment, utensils, linens, or single-use articles.
targetInventory.evidenceCaveat: The Food Code is a model code, not federal law; the depicted shelving is authored outside its warewashing-area exception.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: Clean pans are stored inverted on a separate rack away from the cleaning supplies.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: The pans are food-use equipment on an open rack within the same storage scene.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: They are clean, dry, separated from chemical storage, and inverted, which protects them from contamination.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The pans would become unsafe for use if they were exposed to splash, dust, chemicals, or another contamination source, or were stored wet and unable to drain.
decoyInventory.evidenceCaveat: The Food Code is a model code; the adopting jurisdiction's requirements control.

safeBackground: stable open metal shelving at the upper and center shelves
stable open metal shelving at the lower bowl shelf
requiredCues: vertical alignment clearly puts chemical bottles above uncovered bowls and utensils
containers closed so leakage is not another target
separate safe rack visible
scenes.neutralOverview: A school kitchen storage area with open metal shelving, closed marked supply bottles, uncovered bowls and utensils, and inverted pans.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape school kitchen storage area. On one open shelving unit, several closed generic cleaning-supply bottles occupy the upper shelf directly above uncovered clean mixing bowls and food-preparation utensils on the shelf below. The bottle shapes are generic and have no readable labels. On a separate stable rack, clean pans are stored inverted. The tiled wall and floor are clean and dry.

targetInventory.observableCondition: A connected power cord has a split outer jacket near the plug, with inner insulated conductors visible.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The split outer jacket is an external defect that requires the connected item to be removed from service when the damage may expose a worker to injury.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: If the damage exposes energized conductors, it can cause electrical shock, burns, or fire.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Stop using the item, have it safely de-energized under facility procedure, and remove it from service until repairs and tests render it safe.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: An unused coiled extension cord rests on a broad wall hook and does not cross a walking route.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: Flexible cords can be damaged by improper hanging, fastening, or storage.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: The cord is unused, shows no visible damage, and rests on a broad hook outside the route.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The stored cord would become unsafe if the hook or fastening damaged its jacket, it developed a visible defect, or it was used despite damage.
decoyInventory.evidenceCaveat: No illustration can certify hidden electrical integrity; the cord still requires inspection before future use.

requiredCues: split jacket and inner wires large enough to see
plug visibly seated in outlet
damage isolated from other clutter
scenes.neutralOverview: A dry mechanical room with a portable work light, wall storage, a connected power cord, and a coiled spare cord.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape mechanical utility room. A portable work light stands upright. Its power cord runs a short clear route to a wall receptacle; close to the plug, a large section of the outer jacket is visibly split open and two inner insulated conductors are exposed, while the plug remains connected. A separate undamaged extension cord is neatly coiled on a wall hook. The floor is dry and clear.

targetInventory.observableCondition: A connected power strip lies within a shallow puddle beside the classroom wall.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The authored scenario establishes that the strip is ordinary equipment not approved for wet locations, yet it is connected in a water-inundated conductive location.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: Leakage current through wet equipment can reach a person and cause electrical shock or burns; electrical injuries can be fatal.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Keep people away and have power safely de-energized under facility procedure before handling the equipment; remove the strip from the wet location and do not reuse it until assessed.
targetInventory.evidenceCaveat: Approval status is authored scenario context and is not inferred from the strip's appearance.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: A closed laptop rests on a dry teacher desk with no connection to the puddle shown.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: A laptop is electrical equipment and therefore attracts attention in an electrical-hazard scene.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: For this task, it is closed on a dry desk and has no authored connection to or contact with the puddle.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The laptop setup would become unsafe if it or its ordinary connected power equipment entered water, became likely to contact water without the needed approval, or was used with damage.
decoyInventory.evidenceCaveat: The drawing does not certify every aspect of the laptop's electrical safety.

requiredCues: power strip visibly connected
water contour surrounds strip body
central aisle dry so the puddle is part of the electrical target rather than a separate walking-surface target
scenes.neutralOverview: A classroom with orderly desks, a teacher table, a dry aisle, and electrical equipment near one wall.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape classroom. Desks and chairs are orderly and the central aisle is completely dry. Near the lower-right wall, a plugged-in power strip lies directly within a small shallow puddle whose contour clearly surrounds the strip body; its cord stays along the wall and does not cross the aisle. A closed laptop rests safely on a dry teacher desk.

targetInventory.observableCondition: Several large broken-glass shards are exposed on the restroom floor.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The exposed shards are sharp objects on a walking-working surface.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: A person could suffer a cut, laceration, or puncture wound.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Keep people out of the shard area, then use a broom and dustpan and task-appropriate provided protection—not bare hands—to collect and contain the debris under facility procedure.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: The wall mirror is intact, rounded, and has no visible loose or projecting part.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: The mirror is glass and could create sharp fragments if broken.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: It is intact and has no exposed sharp or protruding part.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The mirror would become unsafe if it cracked, broke, became loose, or exposed a sharp or projecting edge.
decoyInventory.evidenceCaveat: The illustration does not certify hidden mounting strength.

safeBackground: dry floor outside the shard area
requiredCues: recognizable irregular shards with sharp points
shards large enough for phone review
no person handling them
scenes.neutralOverview: A school restroom with a sink, intact wall mirror, stall, waste bin, and several objects on the tile floor.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape school restroom. On the lower-center dry tile floor lie several large irregular broken-glass shards with clearly sharp pointed edges. The wall mirror above the sink is intact and securely mounted. A stall door is closed and an empty lidded waste bin stands upright. No person is present and nothing is wet.

targetInventory.observableCondition: A broken bottle base and exposed shards lie at the edge of the paved school walkway.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The broken bottle leaves sharp glass exposed at the edge of a walking route.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: Someone could step on or contact a shard and suffer a cut.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Keep people out of the shard area, remove and contain every piece, and reopen the route only after it is free of sharp debris.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: A blank closed collection bin stands upright on a concrete pad outside the walking line.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: A collection bin beside a walkway can look like an obstruction or a source of loose waste.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: The bin is closed, upright, and entirely on its pad outside the walking line; no obstruction, leak, or exposed sharp material is shown.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The collection bin would become unsafe if it entered the route, tipped or leaked, or allowed sharp material to protrude.

requiredCues: broken bottle shape and separate sharp shards visible
debris adjacent to and encroaching on the walkway
all other ground even and dry
scenes.neutralOverview: An exterior school walkway beside a building, with a planting bed, a blank closed collection bin, and small objects near the pavement edge.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape exterior school walkway. Near the lower-left edge of the paved route lies a visibly broken glass bottle base and neck fragment with several separate irregular pointed shards extending onto the walkway. The remaining pavement is level and dry. A completely blank closed collection bin stands safely on its own concrete pad; it has no symbol, arrow, text, label, logo, or other marking. A small grounds cart is parked stably on grass outside the route.

targetInventory.observableCondition: A very tall box stack on a small platform dolly leans, with large boxes above smaller visibly compressed boxes.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The load is tall and top-heavy, and its leaning, offset, compressed base is not secure against shifting or collapse.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: Boxes could slide or collapse and strike a worker, especially while the dolly is moved.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Stop moving the load and keep people clear; lower and balance the stack, divide the load, or use suitable handling equipment after confirming stability.
targetInventory.evidenceCaveat: NIOSH guidance is advisory and does not establish one universal handling technique.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: A separate low pallet holds evenly aligned boxes that are fully supported and show no lean or crushed base.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: Any stack of boxes warrants a stability check.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: This stack is low, evenly aligned, fully supported, and shows no lean, crushed base, or shifting.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The pallet stack would become unsafe if its tiers became offset or damaged, its height made it unstable, or it was not secured against sliding or collapse.

safeBackground: parked hand truck upright against wall
requiredCues: leaning centerline obvious
bottom boxes compressed or offset
large boxes at top
dolly fully visible
scenes.neutralOverview: A school loading area with a platform dolly, a low pallet, a hand truck, boxes, and a loading door.
scenes.prompt: Create a wide landscape loading/service area. At center-left, a small platform dolly carries a very tall stack of boxes that visibly leans to one side; two large heavy boxes sit above smaller offset lower boxes, one lower box slightly crushed. A separate pallet holds a low, even, stable stack. A hand truck is upright against the wall and the loading doorway remains fully clear.

targetInventory.observableCondition: A person carries a tall stack of closed boxes above eye level, hiding the route ahead.
targetInventory.whyUnsafe: The boxes block the carrier's eyes and prevent a clear view of the route ahead.
targetInventory.likelyConsequence: The worker could collide with an object or person, trip or fall, or drop the load.
targetInventory.immediateCorrection: Set the load down safely, then divide or repack it, use the nearby cart, or obtain assistance so the route remains visible.
targetInventory.evidenceCaveat: NIOSH guidance is advisory and does not establish one universal carrying technique.

decoyInventory.observableCondition: An empty platform cart is parked stably and parallel to a wall outside the walking route.
decoyInventory.suspiciousBecause: A wheeled cart can become an aisle obstruction if parked carelessly.
decoyInventory.safeAsDepicted: The empty cart is stable, parallel to the wall, and outside the clear walking route.
decoyInventory.unsafeIf: The cart would become unsafe if it rolled or protruded into the aisle, blocked a passage, or carried an unstable load.

requiredCues: full body and both feet visible
boxes cover the person's face and forward view
